command: bench/groot_phases.py --outdir results/20260923_E4d_groot_n17_ladder --checkpoint nvidia/GR00T-N1.7-3B --version n17 --warmup 20 --timed 50 --rung vlm_graphs --tf32 on --head-mode reduce-overhead --llm-mode reduce-overhead
fixture_note: keys and shapes are read from the checkpoint's own processor_config.json and statistics.json; pixel and state VALUES are random, which latency does not depend on
data_processing_note: data_processing_cpu is the checkpoint's own processor + collator, timed separately; e2e below is the GPU path only (model.get_action on already-collated inputs), the same split NVIDIA's benchmark_inference.py reports
vision_note: SUPERSEDED 2026-09-23: vision IS separated now. GR00T's backbone is Qwen3VLForConditionalGeneration, whose .visual and .language_model are the same two parts the LeRobot models expose as embed_image and pg.forward, so vision is timed as a nested region and vlm_prefix is the backbone minus it. GR00T therefore gets the same three-way split as every other model in the study.
